title: White Rice with Cheese and/or Cream Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: White rice prepared with a cheese and/or cream‑based sauce is a nutritious dish enjoyed in many cuisines. The rice provides energy through carbohydrates, while the cheese sauce adds protein, calcium, and a rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is one of the most widely consumed grains worldwide.
Cream sauces are often made from cream, butter, and cheese, giving the dish a smooth texture.
In some cultures rice with cheese sauce is served as a side to meat dishes; in others it is a main course.
Traditional Italian risotto uses a similar concept of rice combined with cheese (Parmesan).
Cream sauces can be flavored with herbs, spices, and garlic for variety.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice supplies complex carbohydrates that provide sustained energy and help maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Protein and calcium
items.content: The cheese sauce contributes dairy protein and calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice contains B1 (thiamine) and B3 (niacin), supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Fatty acids
items.content: Cream sauce adds a modest amount of saturated fats, which can fit into a balanced diet when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Dietary fiber (when using whole‑grain rice)
items.content: A blend of white and whole‑grain rice increases fiber content, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Cream‑based sauces can be rich in saturated fats; individuals with high cholesterol should limit portion size.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese and cream contain lactose; lactose‑intolerant persons should use lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cheese sauces often contain salt; people with hypertension should monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dairy proteins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice topped with hot cheese sauce as a side to meat, fish, or vegetables. Garnish with fresh herbs, green onions, or your favorite spices. For extra flavor, sprinkle grated Parmesan on top.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Keep the sauce separate and reheat before serving. Frozen rice portions remain good for up to 2 months.
